title: Does Anyone Else Make Custom Tools With AI?
author: Blatherbox
selftext:
I was curious if anyone else uses AI to create custom tools to build your games? One area of my game that I wanted to make easier is map making. So I had Claude Code make a map maker/asset library so I could import my assets and build my maps easily. Some of the features I had it add were the ability to use layers with the option to move assets back and forth. As had it add the ability to resize assets with recreating them so they keep their pixel size and not blur the assets. Some other nice features include the ability to edit assets from the library and the ability to flip the assets around. Also I added the option to snap to the grid or the asset next to it which help build floors, and walls. I can create custom sets and categorize the assets (haven't done it yet for the sewer stuff yet) for more organization. It also has the option to import right into unity as well. There is a bunch of other features that I won't get too deep into.

Anyone else have AI create tools for you to make development easier?   
  
I also have some other tools I use as well for posing, some character management, and other little useful tools. I will post two more videos in the comments of a test town scene I made using my map editor showing the game with the rim light, I also turn off and on the rim light in the video so you can see the difference. Also different times of days. The video starts off at night. 

Second video is of the sewer battle you see in the map make with all the changes suggested by the comments from one of my other posts.

comments.author: Destituted
comments.body:
Yep, AI just doesn't get a lot of things, so for the things it doesn't I had it make the tools for me.

Map Editor - This is definitely the hugest one, it has brushes for decor, blending for ground textures, able to place any NPCs and give them conditions on when they'd be visible... tons of other stuff.

Enemy Designer (stats, sprite, movement, skillsets)

Weapon Designer

Quest Designer (let's me write quests myself) that also zooms out to show all of their connections and paths. I can pick pre-set objectives, objective locations or types, all kinds of stuff. Set the conditions that need to be met to become available like a previous quest, set where to get it, where to turn it in at.  It just lists all NPCs and I pick.

Loot Table Designer, I can set loot tables per zone, per monster type, per boss, change the odds, give them chances to have specific materials, etc.

Then for non-UI tools, a Balance Simulator that simulates combat with new enemies I make in like 500 different scenarios to test balance to make sure they're not too easy and not too hard.

replies.author: Blatherbox
replies.body:
That's great I do a lot of the same things. As I mentioned in a previous comment I feel like this is one of the best uses of AI to help make your workflow easier to and create tools that work for you to make it easier.

I should mention I want creative control so I don't want AI making my maps for me for example .. this is one of the reasons I had it make this tool so I can make them faster and with more control and a tool that is custom made for my needs.

Still haven't done the map creator though, was that a big token consumer? I'd assume you had to reiterate through it a few times?

replies.author: Destituted
replies.body:
Yea definitely iteration and a lot of refining things that I refused to just settle on like some live previews of some things.  Fixing performance because it would just render the whole map even when it all wasn’t in view of the editor.

The Map Editor was one of the first things I made so it implemented its hydration system into the game itself, so they basically work together harmoniously since the Map Editor came first.  

The really nice thing is I could clean the map editor up a bit and have players use it to create and share their own maps.
